newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Ofwat calls for more action on metering.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Ofwat calls for more action on metering.

text.p: British water industry watchdog Ofwat called on companies to do more to promote metering on Wednesday as the regulator's report on tariffs was published.
Ofwat head Ian Byatt praised companies which install meters free but said some could do more to promote meters.

"There is widespread customer support (for metering), but customers will only be encouraged to use water wisely if they see the company is also playing its part," Byatt said in a statement to mark the report's publication.

Water conservation through demand management will be one of the subjects of discussion at a conference next Monday called by the new Labour government to address problems caused by Britain's worst drought for 200 years.
Byatt added that companies were also making "considerable progress" towards improving fairness in charging for bills.
Byatt is also encouraging companies to charge customers to ensure users actually pay for the water they use, such as peak tariffs for garden sprinklers.
Ofwat said it would "press companies to make the best possible use of existing resources and to encourage customers to use water wisely."
The driest two years for over 200 years has seen Britain, traditionally a land of mists and rain, drying up and parts of the country already have a ban on using garden hoses.
Ofwat said other important considerations would be "a pro-active approach to leakage control on both the company's and the customer's pipes."
Water and sewerage companies have come under fierce criticism for the amount of water leaking out of pipes, which some estimates put at over 800 million gallons a day.
